preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10⁴) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 2 * 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if (n := int(line.split()[0])) is not None)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10⁵) representing the length of the array a.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(a) == n and all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**9 for x in a) for a in [line.split()[1:] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]] if len(a) == n)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line contains n integers a₁, a₂, ..., aₙ (1 ≤ aᵢ ≤ 10⁹) representing the array elements.
The sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 2·10⁵.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly t lines, one for each test case.
Each output line is a valid integer representing the maximum score for the corresponding test case.

postconditions.expression: all((max_score := max(sum(a[i-1] for i in simulate_path(a, start)) for start in range(1, n+1))) == int(stdout.splitlines()[i]) for i, (n, a) in enumerate(zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]], [line.split()[1:] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]])))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output line is the maximum score achievable by starting at any index i (1 ≤ i ≤ n) and following the game rules, where simulate_path(a, start) returns the sequence of indices visited starting from start, following the movement rule i → i + a[i-1] while i ≤ n.
